purpose: Temporary diagnostic census over the unchanged BTreeMap timer queue algorithm.
byte_order: guest native endian; campaign uses little-endian x86_64
row_order: CPU-major, then manager kind, then field index. CPU identifies execution CPU of each admitted operation, not manager ownership. CPU-time rows combine multiple independently locked managers. Never sum their occupancies and interpret that result as one queue size.

1.name: start
1.ownership: Caller PID owns the new case. Any PID may start after the previous case has stopped successfully and become quiescent.

2.name: stop
2.return: blob_bytes on success; EBUSY requires retry of the same STOP after admission has already closed

3.name: read
3.ownership: Current OWNER PID only; successful quiescent STOP required

arg5: Must be zero for all commands.

modes.0: Gate off, all rows remain zero. Control header still records the case; useful for same-build observer overhead comparison. This is not a pristine-kernel comparison.
modes.1: Counters and histograms only. Timer hooks do not read TSC.
modes.2: Counters, histograms, and elapsed TSC timing. Elapsed includes IRQ, scheduler, virtual-machine, and instrumentation effects; it is not CPU time.

concurrency: Each row and per-CPU ACTIVE are cacheline aligned. Scope disables preemption, increments only its executing CPU ACTIVE, and rechecks the epoch+mode gate before writing. STOP closes the gate and returns EBUSY until all ACTIVE counts are zero. ACTIVE is never reset. START resets only counters after the previous successful quiescent STOP, advances a nonreused epoch, and opens the gate after reset. Delayed old-epoch admissions are rejected without touching rows. User buffers are accessed outside the control lock; READ allocates its buffer before locking. Queue instrumentation accumulates probe/pop/grow counters and length samples locally while the queue guard is held, records its release timestamp, and only then publishes atomic counts and timing buckets. TSC-backward counts are also local until Scope drop.
overflow_cpu: Number of boot-configured CPUs beyond the 64 supported slots. Those CPU operations are not instrumented. A nonzero value means the census is incomplete. This is calculated by control rather than a shared hot-path RMW.
aggregation: Add count/sum/bucket fields across rows; take max for _max fields. Histograms sample individual queues or batches, not manager populations. For one fully admitted cancellation scope: explicit+rearm+owner_drop = weak_upgrade_fail+retire_hit+retire_miss. Dispatch callback outcomes sum to due_pop only when the same dispatch scope is admitted; independently admitted nested periodic rearm/insert scopes may cross window boundaries. Periodic retirement intent equals periodic_retire_hit plus periodic_retire_miss plus periodic_weak_upgrade_fail within each fully admitted periodic cancellation Scope; these fields are explicit-source subsets of the corresponding overall cancellation fields.

fields.name: dispatch_calls
fields.meaning: Calls admitted at process_expired_timers entry.

fields.name: dispatch_empty
fields.meaning: Dispatch calls whose queue is empty at first locked observation.

fields.name: dispatch_nonempty
fields.meaning: Dispatch calls whose queue is nonempty at first locked observation.

fields.name: future_break
fields.meaning: Dispatch loops that encounter a noncancelled minimum with a future deadline and break.

fields.name: min_probe
fields.meaning: Calls to first_key_value inside dispatch, including a final unsuccessful probe. Initial is_empty checks are not probes.

fields.name: insert
fields.meaning: Completed queue insert operations.

fields.name: retire_hit
fields.meaning: Retire remove operations that found the exact callback key.

fields.name: retire_miss
fields.meaning: Retire remove operations that did not find the exact callback key. Attempts equal retire_hit plus retire_miss.

fields.name: weak_upgrade_fail
fields.meaning: Cancel or Timer drop intents that cannot upgrade the callback Weak. These are not retire misses.

fields.name: cancel_explicit
fields.meaning: Calls to public TimerGuard.cancel, counted as method intents before Weak upgrade regardless of queue presence.

fields.name: cancel_rearm
fields.meaning: Calls to set_timeout cancellation, counted as method intents before Weak upgrade, including first arms and periodic rearms.

fields.name: cancel_owner_drop
fields.meaning: Timer destructor intents before Weak upgrade regardless of queue presence.

fields.name: due_pop
fields.meaning: Noncancelled due callbacks popped from the queue into the callback Vec.

fields.name: cancelled_pop
fields.meaning: Cancelled callbacks popped and discarded while holding the queue lock.

fields.name: callback_invoked
fields.meaning: Registered callback invocations after owner upgrade and cancellation arbitration.

fields.name: callback_skip_cancel
fields.meaning: Selected callbacks skipped after owner upgrade because their cancelled flag is set.

fields.name: callback_owner_gone
fields.meaning: Selected callbacks whose owner Weak cannot upgrade at callback invocation time.

fields.name: periodic_rearm
fields.meaning: Selected noncancelled callbacks with nonzero interval, before invoking set_timeout.

fields.name: queue_observations
fields.meaning: Individual queue length observations under the queue lock: before and after insert/remove; at dispatch entry and after nonempty collection.

fields.name: queue_occupancy_sum
fields.meaning: Sum of observed individual queue lengths. This is observation-weighted, not time-weighted and not a population sum across managers.

fields.name: queue_occupancy_max
fields.meaning: Maximum observed individual queue length; aggregate across rows with max rather than sum.

fields.name: batch_observations
fields.meaning: One selected-callback Vec length observation per admitted dispatch, including zero for empty and future-only calls.

fields.name: batch_size_sum
fields.meaning: Sum of selected-callback Vec lengths. Cancelled removals are excluded.

fields.name: batch_size_max
fields.meaning: Maximum selected-callback Vec length; aggregate across rows with max rather than sum.

fields.name: callback_vec_growth
fields.meaning: Push operations that increase the selected-callback Vec capacity while the queue lock is held.

fields.name: callback_vec_capacity_added
fields.meaning: Sum of positive selected-callback Vec capacity increments, measured in Arc slots rather than bytes.

fields.name: tsc_backwards
fields.meaning: Backward consecutive TSC reads within one timing Scope, accumulated locally and published when that Scope exits. Reversed timing pairs are excluded from elapsed statistics; any nonzero count invalidates clean timing interpretation.

fields.name: periodic_retire_intent
fields.meaning: Periodic callback calls into set_timeout cancellation. A subset of cancel_rearm, counted before callback Weak upgrade.

fields.name: periodic_retire_hit
fields.meaning: Retire hits reached from an explicitly tagged periodic rearm; a subset of retire_hit.

fields.name: periodic_retire_miss
fields.meaning: Retire misses reached from an explicitly tagged periodic rearm; a subset of retire_miss. Never inferred from total misses.

fields.name: periodic_weak_upgrade_fail
fields.meaning: Callback Weak upgrade failures reached from explicitly tagged periodic rearm cancellation; a subset of weak_upgrade_fail.

fields.name: reserved_31
fields.meaning: Always zero.

fields.name: queue_hold_tsc_sum
fields.meaning: From immediately after queue lock acquisition until immediately after explicit guard release, including unlock and the guard IRQ-state restoration. A newly enabled interrupt can run before the ending TSC read. Queue observations, probe/pop/grow counts, and timing statistics are published only after this endpoint. This is elapsed lock-region timing, not an exact hardware lock-held or CPU-time measurement.

authorization: INFO is available to any PID. START, STOP, and READ require the existing LSM capable hook to grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace, before census control state is accessed. STOP and READ additionally require the current OWNER PID. An authorized OWNER must finish its case; running cases are not automatically taken over.
